headline: Highest risk is capability conflict from ECC’s filesystem/git write access paired with pdf.js’s browser-based document processing; prompt-injection and leakage are lower because pdf.js is network-isolated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write local files, use MCP, and run browsers, so it could ingest pdf.js outputs if the operator bridges them via files or copy-paste. pdf.js itself only shows browser-based document processing and PDF file I/O, with no direct instruction channel. The pathway exists, but it is not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies pdf.js-rendered text into ECC-managed files or MCP inputs, then prompt injection becomes possible.
IF pdf.js output is treated as instructions by ECC, then malicious PDF content can steer actions.
mitigations: Keep pdf.js outputs in a separate folder from ECC working files.
Disable MCP bridges for untrusted PDF-derived content.
Copy only extracted facts, not raw PDF text, into ECC.
Review any PDF-derived instructions before execution.
Use a manual approval step before ECC acts on pdf.js output.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, git history, and security findings, while pdf.js only touches PDF files and has no network egress. Because pdf.js is network-isolated and no shared workspace is documented, leakage is not evidenced as default; the main risk is accidental local exposure if the operator places sensitive PDFs into ECC-readable paths.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs are stored in a directory ECC reads, then ECC may ingest them into its session or git artifacts.
IF the operator exports pdf.js text into ECC logs or notes, then local leakage occurs.
mitigations: Store sensitive PDFs outside ECC-managed directories.
Redact PDFs before any manual transfer into ECC.
Turn off or review ECC logging for sensitive sessions.
Use separate OS accounts or workspaces for the two tools.
Delete temporary PDF extracts after use.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has filesystem write, git-state modification, subprocess, and allowlisted network egress; pdf.js can run browsers and process PDF files. Even without a documented shared lock, both can act on the same local workspace if the operator points them there, creating overlapping writes and state drift. Uncertainty favors the higher severity because ECC’s write surface is broad.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, then concurrent edits can conflict.
IF ECC modifies git state while pdf.js-derived artifacts are written into the repo, then state drift can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Pause one agent while the other writes files.
Avoid letting pdf.js write into git-tracked paths.
Use git status checks before commits.
Add a simple file-lock or manual handoff step.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC’s workflow surface includes skills, hooks, and MCP, so it can act on imported content; pdf.js produces document text that may be treated as authoritative by the operator or ECC. There is no documented verification barrier between them, so a bad PDF extraction can cascade into downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default use, though not proven by direct evidence.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is fed into ECC without human verification, then extraction errors can propagate.
IF ECC uses PDF-derived text to generate commits, notes, or actions, then downstream mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Verify extracted text against the source PDF.
Require human review before ECC acts on PDF-derived facts.
Use checksum or page-reference checks for critical fields.
Limit ECC to summarization, not action-taking, for PDF inputs.
Keep a traceable link from each claim back to the source page.

E_compliance.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, git history, and security findings, while pdf.js only processes PDF files. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so compliance risk is limited to local handling choices rather than an inherent pairwise violation. The other agent is cited because the risk depends on both data classes and processing surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs are routed into ECC logs or git history, then retention and access controls may diverge.
IF the operator stores PDFs in a jurisdiction-specific workspace, then local policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated PDFs out of ECC logs and git history.
Use a dedicated retention policy for PDF artifacts.
Restrict access to the shared workspace.
Document where PDF-derived data is stored.
Delete temporary exports after review.
